name: Main
description: The landmark that holds the primary content of the page, everything except the shared Header, Navigation and Footer. Use one visible <main> per page.
summary: Landmark for the page's primary content

elements.name: Page content

elements.name: Page heading
elements.description: One h1 that names the page, at or near the start (often in the Hero)

elements.name: Target id
elements.description: An id such as main that the Skip link points to

configOptions.options: Full width (Sections set their own width), Constrained
No, Yes (hidden on inactive views in a single-page app)

variants.caption: Full width — between Header and Footer
Constrained — centered with a maximum width

usageNotes: Use one <main> per page. HTML allows more only when all but one carry the hidden attribute.
Put only content unique to the page inside it. The site Header, Navigation and Footer sit outside, so the banner and contentinfo landmarks stay separate from main.
Place it directly in <body> (a wrapping <div> is fine). HTML does not allow it inside <article>, <aside>, <header>, <footer> or <nav>.
Give it an id and point the Skip link at it, so keyboard users can bypass repeated navigation (WCAG 2.4.1 Bypass Blocks).
Start it with the page's h1, so jumping to the main landmark and jumping to the first heading land in the same place.
